summary: Inishmore Aerodrome (IOR/EIIM) is a small regional airport serving Inis Mór, the largest of the three Aran Islands located in Galway Bay off the west coast of Ireland. The aerodrome provides a vital air link between the island and the mainland, primarily connecting to Connemara and Galway. Its short runway and island setting make it a distinctive gateway to one of Ireland's most culturally rich Gaelic-speaking regions, known for the prehistoric Dún Aonghasa fort and dramatic limestone cliffs.
faqs:
Q: What is the main way to reach Inis Mór?
A: Flights from Connemara Airport (and formerly Galway) on small turboprop aircraft provide the quickest access, typically under 10 minutes from the mainland. Ferry services from Rossaveal also run year-round and take about 40 minutes.

Q: How far is the aerodrome from Kilronan village?
A: The airport is located within walking distance of Kilronan (Cill Rónáin), the island's main port and village, roughly a 15-minute walk or short taxi ride.

Q: Can I book flights online in advance?
A: Yes, scheduled services operated by Aer Arann Islands and partner carriers can be booked through their websites, though seat availability is limited due to small aircraft capacity.

Q: Is the airport affected by weather?
A: Yes, as with all small island aerodromes, flights can be delayed or cancelled due to low cloud, fog, or strong Atlantic winds, so flexible travel plans are recommended.
